fact_text: Over 90 percent of Atlas Honda's bike parts are made locally, because high production volumes make local supplier production viable.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues localisation plus high volume gives Atlas Honda pricing power, and that this shields its per-bike margin from currency devaluation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dealers pay Atlas Honda one to two months before a bike is delivered and delivery itself takes about two months, so dealer advances fund working capital and the company runs a negative cash cycle.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says dealer advances act as free float that the company invests or deposits in banks, adding a return on top of the margin earned on each bike sold.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst compares the negative cash cycle to Apple and Amazon, which also collect customer money early and pay vendors later, and says it compounds with pricing power into multibagger growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Atlas Honda's sales are split between rural and urban buyers, so weak demand in one segment can be offset by the other, the analyst argues.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst claims the CD70 is built in Pakistan at a cost that Chinese bike makers cannot match globally, which he presents as a major competitive advantage.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues bike demand shifts to cars only after GDP per capita rises above roughly 4,000 to 5,000, so a switch to cars is a long-term rather than immediate risk to bike volumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If Pakistan grows around 7 percent a year for a decade, the analyst expects many people to buy their first bike and expects bike sales to peak within that decade if growth continues at 7 to 8 percent.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst estimates plant return on capital by multiplying annual bikes produced by profit per bike and dividing by the plant's cost; at 80 percent utilisation and 15,000 to 20,000 rupees profit per bike he gets roughly 25 to 30 percent.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's long-term thesis is that understanding Atlas Honda as an owner would, through its cost structure, pricing and return on capital, separate it from an average company and drive multibagger returns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The main risk to minority shareholders is the electric transition: the analyst says a competitive EV bike in the 250,000 to 350,000 rupee range is needed, and its absence could hurt returns even while earnings rise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says an EV bike's fuel savings can repay its price premium within six to twelve months, versus four to five years for a car, so he expects a fast transition once EV bike prices are right.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Chinese manufacturers lead in electric two-wheelers, and the analyst sees their EV bike models in Pakistan as competitive pressure on Atlas Honda's planned EV launch.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says Atlas Honda's normal 9 to 10 P/E could compress toward 7 if it fails to launch a competitive EV, because investors discount earnings that a technology shift will erode.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes companies usually get P/E multiples around 8 to 10, and that a company lagging a technology shift that will be adopted in five to six years gets a lower multiple even while current earnings grow.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst projects Atlas Honda selling about 1.4 to 1.6 million bikes over the coming year, with lower steel prices and recent budget duty cuts supporting profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst projects 2026 pre-tax profit of roughly 30 to 35 billion rupees and after-tax profit of about 20 to 22 billion, assuming around 20,000 rupees pre-tax profit per bike.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 earnings per share estimate is roughly 140 to 175 rupees, derived from his after-tax profit projection.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects a dividend of about 70 to 90 rupees in 2026, reflecting a high payout while expansion spending is low.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Atlas Honda's stated dividend policy is a payout of 40 to 60 percent of profit, with the payout nearer 40 percent when the plant nears capacity and expansion spending is needed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Atlas Honda pays an interim dividend with its September results, and a final dividend follows the annual results released around March and is declared around April to May.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Pakistan's bike company - Atlas Honda. Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)
